R E A D T H E R O O M
How Terraform Interviews Work
🧠
P4 · DECODER
Terraform interviews test three things in order: can you define it, can you explain the mechanism, and can you survive the disaster. Most
candidates stop at rung one — this book rungs every question three high.
📋
T H E S H A P E O F T H E I N T E R R O G A T I O N
Round 1 screens definitions (what is state, what does init do). Round 2 probes mechanisms (why a saved plan, what a lock
protects). Round 3 replays disasters (dead CI holder, deleted state, -/+ on a database). Safe answers pass rounds 1–2; only senior
depth closes round 3.
1 The 3-rung decoder
Rung What it is What the interviewer hears
✅
Safe Correct definition, 2 lines “Knows the tool — ask me harder.”
🚀
Senior depth Mechanism + WHY “Has run this in prod — topic closed.”
🚩
Red flag Confident wrong-signal answer “Dangerous near prod — probe deeper.”
🎯
H O W T O C L I M B
Open safe on every question. If the interviewer leans in, spend the senior rung. Never volunteer a red-flag-shaped sentence —
each question below names yours so you can avoid it.
2 The 4 interviewer archetypes
📖
The Definitionalist — “Define state.” Wants crisp sentences. Feed rung 1, stop. Rambling mechanisms here reads as bluffing.
⚙
The Mechanic — “What happens when two applies collide?” Wants the mechanism (locks, bindings, plan files). This is rung 2
territory.
🔥
The Arsonist — “State deleted, prod passionate, go.” Wants calm triage order: inspect, never assume, next plan heals. Never
promise rollback.
🔍
The Auditor — “How does your team gate applies?” Wants PR plan-gate-apply, fmt -check, pinned providers, no committed
secrets. Process answers only.
🚩
U N I V E R S A L R E D F L A G S
“We apply with -auto-approve by hand.” “State is in git so everyone has it.” “Force-unlock first, ask later.” Any one of these can
end an interview on its own.

C A L I B R A T I O N
The 30-Second Answers
⏱
P5 · 6 SCRIPTS
Six answers you must deliver cold, in 30 seconds each. Say the Say line verbatim; the Lands line is why it works.
①
What is Terraform?
Say: “Terraform is HashiCorp's tool for building, changing, and versioning infrastructure — I declare end-state in HCL, it figures out the API calls.
Single Go binary, 2014, one workflow across clouds.”
②
Why not ClickOps?
Say: “Console infra is tribal knowledge — nobody can answer what prod is or who changed it Tuesday. In Terraform, git log answers both, and
every change passes plan review first.”
③
State in one breath?
Say: “State is Terraform's memory: a JSON map of config to real IDs, IPs, and dependencies. Config says what I want, state says what exists, refresh
verifies — delete it and Terraform forgets everything.”
④
Plan before apply?
Say: “Plan previews, apply executes — and apply on a saved plan file runs exactly what was reviewed, no drift window. Bare apply in prod is how
outages happen.”
⑤
Modules?
Say: “Modules package infra like functions — inputs vary per caller, outputs cross the boundary as plain values like module.vpc.vpc_id. Registry
modules get version pins, or upstream edits you at 3 AM.”
⑥
Floci?
Say: “Floci is a local AWS emulator — container on port 4566, dummy creds plus endpoint override. I ran init → plan → apply → destroy against it
and proved idempotence with a clean second plan.”
✓
R E H E A R S A L R U L E
Record yourself. Any answer over 30 seconds is a rung-1 answer with rung-2 fat on it — trim, don't add.

Z O N E 1 · F U N D A M E N T A L S
What Terraform Is & Why It Exists
🟢
Z1 · 6Q
Q1
🔥
? Terraform in one sentence — what is it?
✅
SAFE ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
A tool for building, changing, and versioning infrastructure — declare what you want in config, Terraform makes reality
match.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
HashiCorp, 2014, single Go binary with zero runtime. Manages existing providers (AWS, Cloudflare…) and custom in-house
ones against any API — breadth is the whole point.
🚩
R E D F L A G
“Config manager / AWS-only / container orchestrator” — that's Ansible, CloudFormation, K8s. Naming the wrong layer fails
round 1 instantly.
Q2
🔥
? Declarative vs imperative — which pair is correct?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
Declarative states WHAT (Terraform); imperative scripts HOW (playbooks).
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Terraform takes end-state and derives ordering plus API calls itself — you never write the steps. Playbooks list steps to
execute, with no state to diff against.
🚩
R E D F L A G
The inverted pair (Terraform=HOW). It's the exam's favorite trap shape — interviewers use it the same way.
Q3
🔥
? Same config applied twice — second plan shows…? Why?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy — “No changes.” Healthy steady state.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Idempotence: same code → same infra, re-apply is a no-op by design. Refresh re-read reality, compare found zero drift:
desired == known == real.
🚩
R E D F L A G
“Terraform skips planning” — it planned fully, then did nothing. And “faster on repeat” confuses caching with idempotence.
Q4? AWS + Cloudflare + GitHub in one apply — why Terraform?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
Platform-agnostic: one apply across any providers the moment a second API enters.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
CloudFormation can't leave AWS; splitting tools loses the single plan. Speed, community, practices are all true of Terraform
and all miss the question — scope is the answer.
🚩
R E D F L A G
Answering “it's faster” or “great community” — true, irrelevant, and it tells a Mechanic you dodge scope questions.

Z O N E 2 · S T A T E & B A C K E N D S
Memory, Locks & Ledger Surgery
🟡
Z2 · 8Q
Q1
🔥
? What does terraform.tfstate actually store?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
JSON memory mapping config to real objects: IDs, IPs, ARNs, CIDRs, dependency edges — what the APIs returned after
apply.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Four functions: track (what's mine), compare (desired vs actual → plan diff), metadata (values config never declared),
perform (cache so plan skips re-querying).
🚩
R E D F L A G
“Re-queried live every second, state optional” or hand-editing the JSON — every fix has a state command; hand edits
corrupt.
Q2
🔥
? Five engineers, one local state file — first fix?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
Remote backend. Local + two writers = last apply wins silently, then duplicates.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
S3 + DynamoDB, two jobs: versioned encrypted bucket stores, lock table guards. Backend checklist is all three —
versioning + encryption + locking; one pillar is a half answer.
🚩
R E D F L A G
Committing tfstate to git or emailing it around — state holds secrets in plaintext plus the keys to everything.
Q3? Sensitive values in state — how do you handle them?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
They sit in state — so state never enters git, backend is encrypted, access is restricted.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Leak paths multiply: tfvars values, CI logs echoing outputs raw. Encrypt the backend, mark variables sensitive, keep secrets
out of logs and repos.
🚩
R E D F L A G
“Base64 is encryption” thinking, or terraform output -raw secrets into CI logs.
Q4
🔥
? Second apply starts while the first holds the lock?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
It waits or fails with a lock error — coordinate, queue, serialize. A live lock means a live writer.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Force under a LIVE holder corrupts state for both runners — the cardinal sin. Force is for the dead only; per-env lock tables
isolate blast radius.
🚩
R E D F L A G
“Force-unlock first, ask later.” Uttering this near a live apply ends interviews.
💼

Z O N E 3 · W O R K F L O W & C L I
The Loop: init → plan → apply
🟡
Z3 · 6Q
Q1
🔥
? Fresh clone on a new laptop — first command, and what appears?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
terraform init — downloads provider binaries, installs modules, configures the backend. Nothing works until it runs.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Binaries land in .terraform/ (ignored, re-fetchable); the lock file pins EXACT builds (committed). Bumping a constraint does
nothing until init -upgrade — plan keeps the locked binary.
🚩
R E D F L A G
Planning before init, or committing .terraform/ — megabytes of regret for zero reproducibility.
Q2
🔥
? Core workflow in order?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
Write → init → plan → apply. First word is write — init needs something to install for.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Plan is read-only and safe anytime — run it on every PR. Read the diff symbols: + add, ~ change, - destroy. A -/+ on a
database means stop and snapshot.
🚩
R E D F L A G
“Plan is optional, apply covers it” — apply-without-plan is the anti-pattern in prod.
Q3? Why apply a saved plan file instead of bare apply?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
apply tfplan executes EXACTLY the reviewed diff — what you saw is what runs, no drift window.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
PR → plan posted → merge → gated apply: infra gets code-review discipline. -out serializes any plan, including destroy
previews (plan -destroy -out).
🚩
R E D F L A G
Auto-apply on merge skipping human review — the pipeline judges what nobody read.
Q4? Apply interrupted halfway (Ctrl+C) — what is true?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
Partial stands — finished creates stay, state is written incrementally. Next plan reconciles. Never promise rollback.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Failed apply guarantees nothing about the world: inspect state AND reality, then let the next plan heal. Hand-typed -auto-
approve in prod is how the interruption finds you.
🚩
R E D F L A G
“All-or-nothing rollback” or “retry resumes where it stopped” — both fictions; re-entry is a fresh plan.
Q5? fmt vs validate in CI — which gate does what?
💼

Z O N E 4 · V A R I A B L E S & C O N F I G
Inputs, Precedence & Types
🟡
Z4 · 6Q
Q1
🔥
? Defaults, TF_VAR, terraform.tfvars, -var all set — who wins?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
-var wins. Ladder top-down: CLI flags → files → env vars → defaults. Value surprise? Strip top-down; the stray flag is the
prime suspect.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Env sits BELOW files, not above — the classic inversion. Per-team sizes come from variables with per-caller values, never
from copied repos or console edits.
🚩
R E D F L A G
“Env beats files” or “defaults override” — reciting the ladder backwards fails the easiest senior probe there is.
Q2? terraform.tfvars vs *.auto.tfvars — the difference?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
terraform.tfvars is the single auto-loaded values file; *.auto.tfvars are layered overlays loaded lexically in name order.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Explicit -var-file vs automatic layering: overlays stack (base.auto.tfvars → prod.auto.tfvars), so later names win. One file can't
layer; overlays can't be explicit.
🚩
R E D F L A G
Secrets in either file committed to git — layering doesn't launder credentials.
Q3? What gets committed: real tfvars or the example?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
Template shared, secrets local: commit *.tfvars.example, ignore real *.tfvars.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Full gitignore canon: ignore .terraform/, tfstate (+backup), real tfvars. Commit lock file + versions.tf — reproducibility is the
half interviewers grade.
🚩
R E D F L A G
“Commit tfvars so the team stays in sync” — sync via the example, never via values.
Q4? TF_VAR_tags for a map variable — exact syntax?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
Single-quoted HCL: TF_VAR_tags='{Env="prod"}' — shell-safe quoting so braces survive.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Same rule for objects. Bare braces split on spaces, double quotes interpolate — both corrupt before Terraform ever sees
the value.
🚩
R E D F L A G
Unquoted complex TF_VAR and “Terraform parsed it wrong” — the shell ate it, not Terraform.
Q5? TF VAR count="three" on a number var — result? And for each over a bare list?
💼

Z O N E 5 · R E S O U R C E S & L O G I C
Count, for_each & Providers
🔁
6 Q · IDENTITY IS EVERYTHING
📋
T H E O N E L E S S O N
Under count, the index is the identity — remove the middle and everything after shifts. Under for_each, the key is the identity —
edits touch one instance only. Say that sentence and half this zone answers itself.
Q1
🔥
count vs for_each — when do you use which?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
count clones N identical copies addressed web[0], web[1]; for_each stamps one instance per key, addressed web["blue"].
Copies → count; named things → for_each.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Index identity vs key identity: deleting web[1] under count renames web[2]→web[1] and rebirths the tail; under for_each
only that key is destroyed. Only keys survive reordering — that is why sets/maps, never lists, feed for_each.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"They're interchangeable" — signals you've never removed an item from the middle of a counted fleet and watched the
cascade in the plan.
Q2
🔥
for_each over a bare list fails. Fix?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
for_each needs a set or map. Wrap it — for_each = toset(var.list) — or build a key map. Lists re-index, so they can't
supply stable identity.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
toset() casts list → stable set so each value becomes its own key; for richer objects, a map gives you each.key / each.value
with per-field types. Duplicates collide at plan time — that error is the identity check working.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"Just use count instead, always" — dodges the identity problem instead of solving it; the next edit rebirths the fleet.
Q3 count = 3 → count = 2. What gets destroyed?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
web[2] — the tail. Count removes from the end; web[0] and web[1] are untouched.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
The corollary is the real interview answer: removing from the middle (targeted destroy of web[1]) shifts every later index
and rebirths the tail. for_each keys don't shift — the exam's core repetition lesson, and the reason fleets use keys.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"web[0]" or "all three" — guessing reveals you've never read a count-shrink plan line by line.
Q4 How do you make a resource conditional, and read it safely?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
count = var.on ? 1 : 0 toggles one instance; read it with one(x[*].attr) — null when off. Never index x[0] directly: it
explodes when the resource is absent.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
💼

Z O N E 6 · M O D U L E S
Consume, Author, Version
📦
6 Q · CONTRACT: SOURCE + IN + OUT
📋
T H E C O N T R A C T
Every module call is three parts: source (where the code lives), inputs (what you feed it), outputs (what it hands back). A fourth
invented part — credentials inside, state inside — always marks the distractor.
Q1
🔥
How does a stack consume module outputs?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
As a normal reference — module.vpc.private_subnets[0] is a value like any other. Root calls children; children expose
outputs the root consumes. Outputs flow upward only.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Outputs are the module's public API: they turn internal resource attributes into typed, documented values downstream
code, other modules, and CI can rely on. "Display-only" or "console-only" answers confuse output blocks with terraform
output reads.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"Only via remote state" — remote state wires stacks, not modules. Reaching across stacks for what an output already hands
you is architecture by accident.
Q2
🔥
Pin a registry module to 5.x. Exact block — and the risk if version is missing?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
source + version = "5.1.0" (or ~> 5.0). Source says WHERE, version says WHICH. Missing version floats — a future major
can break runs that changed nothing.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Pinning without a source is a wish; sourcing without a pin is a gamble. Local paths take no version key (no registry to
resolve); git URLs pin commits, not registry versions. For a bug-fix bump, pin the patched minor explicitly — review majors
by hand.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"The registry pins automatically" — it doesn't. That sentence has caused more surprise majors than any other in this
ecosystem.
Q3 Which module sources are valid?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
Local paths, public/private registry, git URLs, HTTP/S3 archives — not just the public registry, not Docker Hub. Installed
copies land in .terraform/modules after init.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Init collision errors come from .terraform/modules, never the registry — two copies of one source collide locally; the
registry is remote and read-only. New module + weird behavior → "did you init?" — apply only runs installed code.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"Only the public registry" — rules out every enterprise pattern (private registry, mono-repo local paths) in one breath.
Q4 Should child modules declare provider blocks?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
Avoid it inherit from the root Provider config flows DOWN never as a module input; required providers declare the

Z O N E 7 · L I F E C Y C L E & G U A R D S
Gates, Locks & Safe Surgery
🛡
6 Q · FIVE-GATE PIPELINE
📋
T H E F I V E G A T E S
fmt -check → init → validate → apply → plan (idempotent, no drift). Style, wiring, syntax, execution, proof. Name all five and
the interviewer knows you've shipped, not just studied.
Q1
🔥
CI must fail on unformatted HCL without rewriting. Command — and validate's job?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
terraform fmt -check — exit 1 on any unformatted file, zero writes. validate checks syntax + consistency with zero cloud
contact: no credentials, no network.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Gate = -check (rewrites belong on laptops); format-on-save + CI -check covers prevention and enforcement. validate
parses, resolves references, type-checks — anything needing AWS (refresh, diffs, costs) is outside its universe. -recursive
covers subfolders; -diff previews.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"Bare fmt in CI" — gates must not mutate. A gate that rewrites is a race with the checkout it runs on.
Q2 Second apply starts while the first holds the lock. What happens?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
It fails with a lock error naming the holder and lock ID — no parallel writes, no merges. Locks are protective, not
punitive.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
One lock table per env buys parallel applies across envs at the cost of more tables to guard; delete the table and applies
run unlocked — last writer wins, silently. Lock fights mean a second writer: coordinate, don't force.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"Re-run with -auto-approve until it passes" — retries collide again without coordination, and -auto-approve near a lock
fight is how two writers become zero states.
Q3
🔥
Lock held by a dead CI runner. Exact recovery?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
Confirm death, then force-unlock by ID, then prove health. Verify no live process holds it first — stale crash, then
release.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Force under a live holder corrupts state for both runners — the cardinal sin. Deleting the DynamoDB row destroys locking
for everyone; restoring backups fixes state, and the lock isn't state. Sequence it: prove dead → unlock by ID → plan clean
before any apply.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"Delete the lock row by hand" or "destroy and recreate the bucket" — surgery for a splinter, with blast radius across every
team sharing the backend.
Q4 Why plan -out=tfplan + apply tfplan instead of bare apply?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
apply tfplan executes EXACTLY the saved plan reviewed == executed no drift between review and run Bare apply re
💼
Terraform Interview Arsenal — Page 12 —
▤
TOC prev | next
Z O N E 8 · M U L T I - E N V & S C A L E
Workspaces, TF_VAR & the ALB Stack
🌍
6 Q · ONE CODEBASE, THREE ENVS
📋
T H E M E N T A L M O D E L
Workspaces isolate state, not code — one configuration, N state files under terraform.tfstate.d/<name>/. Per-env differences
ride variables and terraform.workspace lookups, never copied folders.
Q1
🔥
workspace show vs list — and which workspace can't be deleted?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
show prints only the active name ("where am I"); list prints all names. default is implicit and permanent — it survives every
delete attempt.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Deleting default would strand unscoped state, so migrate away from it instead. A brand-new workspace starts with empty
state — first plan wants to create everything, which is exactly the surprise that bites during demos.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"Workspaces isolate code / providers / regions" — they isolate state. Regions live in provider blocks, code is shared; that's
the entire point.
Q2 What is terraform.workspace in code, and what's the idiom?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
A read-only string of the active name — the key into per-env maps: locals { env = terraform.workspace }, then lookup
sizes, CIDRs, tags. Derive, don't repeat.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Single source per env: one map keyed by workspace beats conditionals scattered across resources. It never lists, versions,
or addresses anything — backends come from blocks, resources from state, versions from the lock file.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"Use it for backend config" — backend blocks can't use var.* or workspace expressions; backend args come from -
backend-config files.
Q3
🔥
Defaults, TF_VAR, terraform.tfvars, -var all set region. Winner — and the TF_VAR map gotcha?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
-var wins. Ladder top-down: CLI flags → files (incl. *.auto.tfvars overlays) → TF_VAR_* env → defaults. Value surprise? Strip
layers top-down; the stray flag is the prime suspect.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
TF_VAR maps need single-quoted HCL (shell-safe object syntax — bare braces split, double quotes interpolate). A variable
with no default and nothing provided prompts — which hangs CI; always feed it via -var/env/file.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"Env vars beat files" — inverted ladder. Misordering the ladder means debugging values in exactly the wrong direction.
Q4 tfvars discipline: what gets committed, what never does?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
Commit *.tfvars.example; ignore real *.tfvars, .terraform/, local state + backup. *.auto.tfvars loads automatically vs
explicit -var-file — know which magic is active.

TFC, Sentinel & Secrets
☁
6 Q · REVIEWED == EXECUTED
📋
T H E G O V E R N A N C E T R I A N G L E
Blessed code (private registry) + locked versions (pins) + enforced rules (Sentinel) + secret-free repos (env/Vault). Miss one side
and the other three can't save you.
Q1 TFC vs TFE — and what does a TFC workspace bind?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
TFC = SaaS hosted by HashiCorp; TFE = self-hosted in your boundary. A TFC workspace binds config + variables +
state + run history — run history lives there, not on laptops.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Heavy teams outgrow the free tier into paid runners/agents: remote operations run on your infra via agents, so plans
execute identically for every engineer. "Just the CLI binary" or "display only" answers miss that the workspace is the
collaboration unit.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"TFE is older Terraform" — confuses a deployment model with a version. Says you've never had to place a compliance
boundary.
Q2
🔥
PR opened → plan posted back → merge → apply. Name it and defend it.
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
VCS-driven runs. Remote runs fire on VCS events; the speculative plan lands as a PR comment with zero state risk; merge
gates the apply.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
Speculative plans analyze the plan remotely — same engine feeds cost estimates on the PR. Golden rule: infra change
without a PR is an incident report waiting for a timestamp. Console runs, local-exec, and state mv are unrelated machinery.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"We apply from laptops, it's faster" — speed that skips review, audit trail, and identical execution is the thing governance
exists to kill.
Q3
🔥
Sentinel: mandatory vs soft-mandatory vs advisory?
✅
S A F E ( J UN I O R→ M I D)
Missing cost tags, no override → mandatory: never passes. Soft-mandatory: passes only with an override by someone
holding the right; advisory: warns, never blocks.
🚀
S E N IO R DE P T H
The axis is override possibility — permitted vs never — not speed or language. Design rules so the common path flows
(advisory for new standards, soft-mandatory during rollout, mandatory once the org can comply), or engineers route
around the policy system entirely.
🚩
R E D F L A G
"Everything mandatory" — a policy set nobody can satisfy is a policy set everybody bypasses. Governance that blocks work
gets uninstalled.
Q4 Where do secrets actually live — state, tokens, CI creds?
✅
SA F E ( J U NI O R →M I D )

W1 init → AccessDenied / hangs. 2 AM, pipeline red.

T R I AG E
floci status → check provider.tf endpoints → confirm dummy creds exported. Cause: emulator not running or endpoint

F I X + P RE V E NT
floci start, verify endpoint lines, re-init. Prevent: health-check the emulator before init in the wrapper script so CI fails fast

W2 plan hangs forever — no output, no error.
✅
T R I AG E
curl the health endpoint → floci status → diff provider.tf endpoint lines vs the live port. Cause: endpoint points at a
dead port / missing line.
🚀
F I X + P RE V E NT
Fix the endpoint, re-plan. Prevent: fail-fast connectivity probe at the top of run scripts; never let plan be the first thing that
touches the network.
W3
🔥
apply is creating REAL AWS resources — real bill accruing.
✅
T R I AG E
Ctrl-C / cancel the run → env | grep -i aws (which profile/creds are live?) → inspect endpoint lines in provider.tf. Cause:
endpoint missing + real profile active.
🚀
F I X + P RE V E NT
Destroy what escaped, confirm endpoints + dummy creds, never mix a real profile into emulator runs. Prevent: explicit
endpoint assertion + deny-real-account guard before every non-prod apply.

✅
T R I AG E
Re-run ls with the same --endpoint-url + region + test creds → compare URL against provider.tf → terraform show to

F I X + P RE V E NT
Align the CLI invocation with the provider config — the resource is real, you're looking through the wrong window.
Prevent: one env file sourced by both Terraform and CLI wrappers.

T R I AG E
terraform state list (empty?) → check backend config / state path → state pull for any surviving snapshot. Cause: two
backend configs, or the ledger is gone.

VCS-driven runs (speculative plan on PR, zero state risk) → Sentinel (advisory→soft-mandatory→mandatory rollout)

Question Answer
Second apply, no edits — plan says? 0/0/0, "No changes" — idempotence, the healthy steady
state.
First command in a fresh clone? init — providers + modules + backend + lock file.
File that guarantees identical providers? .terraform.lock.hcl — commit it; ignore .terraform/.
File that must NEVER be committed? terraform.tfstate — plaintext secrets + keys to everything.
validate proves what, touching what? Syntax + consistency, zero cloud contact.
CI style gate without rewriting? fmt -check — exit 1, no writes.
Write → ? → ? → ? write → init → plan → apply.
Reviewed == executed — how? plan -out=tfplan → apply tfplan.
for_each accepts…? Set or map — bare lists wrap with toset().
web["blue"] implies…? for_each keys — string-key identity.
count 3→2 destroys…? web[2] — the tail; middle removal cascades.
Safe read of a 0/1 counted resource? one(x[*].attr) — null when off.
Nested-block repetition lives where? dynamic blocks — data in, stanzas out.
Cross-region block selects how? provider = aws.eu — aliased instance.
Registry module pin = ? source + version — one without the other is a gamble.
Installed modules land where? .terraform/modules — collisions happen there.
show vs list (workspaces)? show = active name; list = all names.
Workspace you can't delete? default — implicit and permanent.
-var vs TF_VAR vs files? -var > files > TF_VAR > defaults.
Rename with zero rebuild? state mv — new address, same object.
rm vs destroy? rm forgets (lives); destroy deletes (dies).
Dead-holder lock recovery? Confirm death → force-unlock by ID → plan clean.
PR → posted plan → merge → apply? VCS-driven runs — speculative, zero state risk.
Mandatory vs soft-mandatory? Override: never vs permitted — advisory only warns.

Checklist & Trap Radar
🌙
DEPLOY YOURSELF
✅
N I G H T - B E F O R E C H E C K L I S T
Run it in order. Sleep beats cramming after box 6.
Pre-flight (do tonight)
Five-gate pipeline cold: fmt -check → init → validate → apply → plan (no drift).
One-liners ready: 0/0/0, lock.hcl, toset(), state mv, -var ladder, VCS-runs.
Numbers memorized: dev vpc-5e7eebfd 6-added · staging/prod 22-added · EC2 stub code 48.
Two stories rehearsed aloud: one triage (W1–W8), one design (fleet or pipeline).
Laptop rules: no -auto-approve by hand, no real profile near emulator dirs, creds via env.
Morning-of (before you leave)
Say the identity sentence once: "Index is identity under count; key is identity under for_each."
Say the governance triangle once: blessed code + locked versions + enforced policy + secret-free repos.
Pick your closer: one incident you survived, 30 seconds, with the prevention you added.
🎯
T R A P R A D A R — 6 R U L E S
Trap Rule
1 · EXCEPT / NOT stems Invert first: cover the answers, ask "which one doesn't belong" — e.g. state purposes EXCEPT
compiling HCL. Most misses are right answers to the wrong question.
2 · Workspace homonyms Three different things share the name: CLI workspaces (state isolation),
terraform.workspace (a string key), TFC workspaces (config+vars+state+runs). Ask which
one before answering.
3 · -var precedence Ladder: -var > files > TF_VAR > defaults. Value surprise? Strip top-down — the stray flag is
always the prime suspect, env never beats files.
4 · Sensitive-display myth sensitive masks, never encrypts — plaintext stays in state; -raw to logs still leaks. Real
protection is bucket+IAM, Vault/SSM, and ephemeral for same-apply reads.
5 · Count-vs-key identity [0] vs ["az"]: only keys survive reordering. Any stem with removal/reorder/shrink → answer in
identity terms, then name the cascade (count) or the isolation (for_each).
6 · Skipped-plan stems "Straight to apply", "no review", "laptop -auto-approve" → the answer is always the saved
plan + gate: plan -out, review, apply tfplan, VCS-driven runs in prod. Speed is never the
control.
💬
T H E C L O S E R
"Safe gets me to the next question; senior ends the topic." Climb every question until the interviewer nods and moves on — the
nod is the deploy confirmation.
